title: Choose the visual world for the dashboard (second hand)
question: The re-roll assigned the Marey Timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Marey Timetable
options.lineage: E. J. Marey's 1880s Paris–Lyon train graph, the chart Tufte made famous
options.thesis: Each PR is a train through five stations; flat runs are waiting, steep runs are moving, so the eye sees where time goes before reading a number.
options.viewport: A full-width timetable: stations ready, response, lgtm, approved, merged run down the left; hundreds of PR lines cross them, piling into long flat runs at lgtm; the sentence 'Review is where PRs wait' sits above, the top two queues called out in red.
options.risk: Dense line charts can read as noise on a phone; the graph needs a calm default and a plain-language key or it loses the 30-second reader.

raised.raise: A still default state: the graph reads fully with no motion or interaction.
Every figure carries a plate number and a source line (snapshot date, PR count).
No boxes or cards: structure comes from rules and baselines, and rank is carried by ink weight.
Every state has a named, text-equivalent label, so colour is never the only signal.

options.label: Blameless Postmortem
options.lineage: SRE postmortem documents (Google SRE book), the TPM's own ritual
options.thesis: The snapshot written as a blameless postmortem: summary, impact, where time went, contributing factors, and what the data can't tell you.
options.viewport: A one-page document header (title, snapshot date, author, status), a three-line summary of the finding, then an impact table and a timeline of where a PR's 7.3 days go.
options.risk: Familiar to engineers and TPMs, and close to what many incident write-ups look like; it can read as a document rather than an interactive tool.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: A centre staff read upward: the author's moves on one side, reviewers' on the other, each block as long as the wait.
options.viewport: One score per ranked queue, whose-move split left and right, time rising up the page.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: whose move maps to its left and right columns and duration to block length; loses on audience, since few readers know dance notation.
options.risk: Reads as an art piece without a key.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: Review drawn as rooms in a building section, with light reaching some and not others.
options.viewport: A building section with one room per stage.
options.case: The metaphor needs explaining before the data does.

options.label: Design Annual Plate Section
options.thesis: Each chart presented as a printed plate with registration marks and credits.
options.viewport: A grid of plates, one per finding.
options.case: Reads as a design portfolio, not an analysis.
options.kept: Plate numbers and source lines on every figure.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller Queue
options.thesis: Queues as layered lines of bitmap text over a black void, rank as depth.
options.viewport: A ranked queue list floating in layers.
options.case: Neither audience shares the demoscene's references, and motion fights reading.
options.kept: No boxes; rank carried by ink.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Stages as horizon bands moving from night to day.
options.viewport: Bands for each stage, brighter when PRs move.
options.case: Atmosphere without a route to ranking queues.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An engineering-metrics dashboard: KPI tiles, bar charts and a sortable table, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Headline tiles, then the brief, the ranked table and the charts, as the page looks today.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every analytics product by design.
